answers.primary: A project CLAUDE.md committed to the repo at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, holding the short concrete facts: build with `pnpm build:all`, tests need a local Postgres, API handlers live in `src/api/handlers/`. Seed it with `/init` and keep it under about 200 lines so adherence stays high.
answers.rejected_alternative: Auto memory. Claude's own MEMORY.md is machine-local under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ and never travels through version control, so every teammate would rebuild the same notes independently.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. CLAUDE.md is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, so it is context that shapes behavior rather than configuration the harness enforces.
answers.context_boundary: It loads into the main session context at launch, ordered from the filesystem root down to the working directory and after user-scope CLAUDE.md. It also reaches every custom and built-in subagent except the built-in Explore and Plan agents, which skip CLAUDE.md and git status.
answers.lifecycle: Loads at the start of every session started anywhere in that directory tree, and the project-root file is re-read from disk and re-injected after `/compact`. It stops applying if a path matches `claudeMdExcludes` or if `project` is dropped from `--setting-sources`.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open: nothing blocks a session that ignores it, and adherence degrades as the file grows past a couple of hundred lines or accumulates vague or contradictory entries. Confirm it actually loaded by running `/context` and checking the Memory files list.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate for a plain project CLAUDE.md. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 turns `/init` into an interactive multi-phase flow that also proposes skills and hooks, and the `/doctor` trim suggestion for an oversized checked-in CLAUDE.md requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later.

answers.primary: A skill at .claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md invoked as `/release-notes`, with the fixed template and the long-form conventions moved into supporting files in the skill directory, and the changelog query wired in either as a `` !`command` `` dynamic-context injection or as a bundled script pre-approved with `allowed-tools: Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/changelog.sh *)`.
answers.rejected_alternative: Putting the procedure in CLAUDE.md. A 30-step playbook used once a week would sit in the context window of every session, paying full token cost for the vast majority of sessions that are not a release.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. The harness renders the file, substitutes arguments and runs the injected shell commands, but nothing checks that Claude actually walked all 30 steps or honored the template.
answers.context_boundary: Only the name and description live in the skill listing until invocation; the rendered SKILL.md body then enters the main conversation as a single message and stays for the rest of the session. Supporting files cost nothing until Claude reads them, and adding `context: fork` would move execution into a subagent so only the finished notes come back.
answers.lifecycle: Runs when you type `/release-notes` or when Claude matches your request to the description. The content persists across turns, and after auto-compaction the most recent invocation is re-attached with its first 5,000 tokens inside a shared 25,000-token budget, so a long session may drop it and need a re-invoke.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open. The realistic failure in a 30-step procedure is silent step-skipping or template drift, especially late in a session or after compaction; nothing verifies the output shape, so pair it with a checklist at the end of the skill or a review step.
answers.version_caveat: Keep SKILL.md under about 500 lines and push detail into supporting files. `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` substitution inside `allowed-tools` requires v2.1.129 or later, `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` requires v2.1.196, and `background: false` on a forked skill requires v2.1.218. A managed `disableSkillShellExecution: true` would neuter the changelog injection.

answers.primary: A user-invocable skill at .claude/skills/reseed-staging/SKILL.md with `disable-model-invocation: true`, encoding the drop-and-reseed steps once and run as `/reseed-staging`, with `allowed-tools` scoped narrowly to the specific reseed script rather than to Bash generally.
answers.rejected_alternative: An MCP server tool wrapping the reseed script. Any tool exposed to the model is a tool the model can decide to call on its own, so you would immediately need a separate permission rule to hold the same line the frontmatter flag holds for free.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split, and the split is the point. The harness owns the invocation gate: with `disable-model-invocation: true` the skill's description is kept out of Claude's context and the Skill tool cannot reach it, so the assistant cannot elect to reseed. The model still owns faithful execution of the steps once you trigger it.
answers.context_boundary: Nothing about this skill occupies the main context until you type the command. On invocation the rendered body enters the main conversation and stays for the session; it is also excluded from being preloaded into subagents.
answers.lifecycle: Only your explicit `/reseed-staging` starts it. The flag also prevents it from running when a scheduled task fires with the skill as its prompt. It stops applying if someone removes the flag, or if `skillOverrides` or permission rules change its visibility.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on triggering, which is the desired direction: the worst case is that Claude will not offer or start a reseed even when one is genuinely wanted, and a human has to type the command. The destructive steps themselves remain advisory once invoked, so back them with an `ask` or `deny` permission rule on the actual drop command if an accidental invocation would be costly.
answers.version_caveat: The frontmatter flag blocking scheduled-task firing requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later. Frontmatter booleans other than `true`/`false` (yes/no/on/off/1/0) are only accepted from v2.1.218. As an alternative that needs no file edit, `skillOverrides` can set the skill to `user-invocable-only` from .claude/settings.local.json.

answers.primary: A path-scoped rule file at .claude/rules/api-conventions.md with `paths: ["src/api/**/*.ts"]` frontmatter, carrying the input-validation, standard-error-envelope and OpenAPI-comment requirements so they load only when Claude touches that package.
answers.rejected_alternative: Another section appended to the root CLAUDE.md. It is already at its useful size limit, and more always-resident text is precisely what is eroding adherence for everything else in the file.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. Rules are the same class of thing as CLAUDE.md, context injected into the conversation, not configuration the client enforces.
answers.context_boundary: Main conversation only, and it loads lazily: the rule enters context the first time Claude reads a file matching the glob, not on every tool call, so sessions that never open src/api pay nothing for it.
answers.lifecycle: Triggers on the first matching file read and then stays available for the rest of the session. It stops applying if `project` is excluded from `--setting-sources`, if the file is caught by `claudeMdExcludes`, or if the glob stops matching after a directory move.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open, with a specific gap: if Claude creates a brand-new endpoint file without first reading an existing file under src/api, the rule may never load at all. A malformed glob, for example an unescaped `[`, matches nothing silently while the rule's other patterns keep working.
answers.version_caveat: Path matching through a symlinked checkout requires v2.1.198 or later. Brace expansion in `paths` shares a 1,000-pattern / 4 MiB budget and oversized lists were a startup stall or crash before v2.1.217; an invalid bracket pattern broke the Read tool for every evaluated file before v2.1.207; and before v2.1.211 on-demand rules loaded even when `project` was excluded from setting sources.

answers.primary: User-scope memory on that engineer's machine: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or better, split by topic into `~/.claude/rules/` files (indentation, conventional-commit format, preferred diff-review flow) so each stays short and editable.
answers.rejected_alternative: A project CLAUDE.md or a committed .claude/rules file. That is the wrong scope by definition: anything checked in imposes one person's formatting and commit habits on every teammate who opens the repo.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. These are preferences delivered as context; nothing in the harness makes an indentation or commit-message convention stick.
answers.context_boundary: Loads into the main context of every session on that machine, first in the CLAUDE.md load order so project instructions can still override it, and user-level rules load before project rules. Imports inside user-scope memory load without the external-import approval dialog because they are files the user wrote.
answers.lifecycle: Every session start on that machine, in every repository, until the engineer edits or deletes the files. A conflicting project instruction, loaded later and closer to the working directory, effectively supersedes it for that repo.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open. Two live risks: a project CLAUDE.md that says something different leaves the model picking arbitrarily, and formatting preferences lose to whatever the repo's formatter or commit hook actually does. If the diff-review flow must actually happen every time, only a hook will guarantee it.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate. Worth knowing that `~/.claude/` configuration does not reach Cowork sessions, cloud sessions or routines, and that a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md exists only in the worktree where it was created, which is exactly why home-directory user scope is the right home for machine-wide personal preferences.

answers.primary: Auto memory, left enabled so Claude writes its own notes to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, keeping a concise MEMORY.md index and pushing detail into topic files like flaky-tests.md and dev-environment.md; audit and prune it with `/memory`.
answers.rejected_alternative: A CLAUDE.md that the team maintains by hand. It would hold exactly the same facts, but it requires a human to write, update and prune it, which is the explicit thing nobody wants to do.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. Claude decides what is worth remembering, when to write it, and when to read a topic file back; the harness only supplies the directory and the load limits.
answers.context_boundary: Main conversation only. The first 200 lines or 25 KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, is loaded at every session start; topic files are read on demand with normal file tools. The main conversation's auto memory is not passed to subagents, except a fork; a subagent needs its own `memory` field for a separate directory.
answers.lifecycle: Writes happen mid-session whenever Claude judges something reusable, prompted by your corrections. It loads at the start of every session for that git repository and is shared across all its worktrees and subdirectories. It stops if `autoMemoryEnabled` is set to false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 is set.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open, and it is machine-local: the accumulated knowledge never reaches teammates, CI, or cloud sessions. It can also record a fact that was true once and keep asserting it, and anything past the 200-line / 25 KB index limit is silently dropped at load unless MEMORY.md is kept trimmed.
answers.version_caveat: The near-limit reminder and over-limit rewrite error require v2.1.210; excluding frontmatter and HTML comments from that measurement requires v2.1.211; and the `modified` ISO 8601 timestamp on memory files requires v2.1.214. An `autoMemoryDirectory` set in a project's settings is honored only after you accept that folder's workspace trust dialog.

answers.primary: A custom output style, a markdown file in .claude/output-styles/ (or ~/.claude/output-styles/ for the individual) containing the calm runbook voice and the fixed response structure, with `keep-coding-instructions` left at its default of false so Claude Code's built-in software-engineering instructions are dropped from the system prompt. Select it with `/config`, or set `"outputStyle"` in a settings file for the whole group.
answers.rejected_alternative: CLAUDE.md. It appends a user message after the system prompt and can add tone guidance, but it cannot remove the built-in software-engineering instructions, which is exactly the part that keeps pulling answers back toward code changes.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. The harness deterministically assembles the system prompt and omits the coding instructions, but every-turn adherence to voice and structure is the model's.
answers.context_boundary: Appended to the end of the main conversation's system prompt. It does not apply to subagents, which run their own system prompts; a fork of the conversation is the only exception.
answers.lifecycle: Read once at session start and in force for every response, with periodic reminders to adhere. A change to the style or the setting takes effect only after `/clear` or a new session, and it stops applying when a different style is selected.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open: the voice can drift over a long conversation, and anything produced by a subagent comes back in the default voice. Dropping the coding instructions is also all-or-nothing, so if this group ever does need code help in the same session they have to switch styles and restart.
answers.version_caveat: The standalone `/output-style` command was deprecated in v2.1.73 and removed in v2.1.91; use `/config` or the `outputStyle` setting. Shipping the style in a plugin allows `force-for-plugin: true`, which applies it automatically whenever the plugin is enabled and overrides the user's own `outputStyle`; nested project style directories resolve to the one closest to the working directory as of v2.1.178.

answers.primary: A PreToolUse hook matching Bash (and PowerShell where relevant) that reads the command plus the resolved target branch from stdin and returns `permissionDecision: "deny"` (or exits 2) for any push that would land on main, registered in managed policy settings so it applies to every session on every machine.
answers.rejected_alternative: A `permissions.deny` rule such as `Bash(git push *)`. It is also client-enforced, but argument-shaped Bash patterns are fragile and cannot see which branch a bare `git push` will resolve to, so it either over-blocks every push or misses forms like a push with an upstream already configured.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. The hook is a shell command run at a fixed lifecycle event and applies regardless of what the model decides, which is precisely why the instruction file failed and this will not.
answers.context_boundary: It runs outside the model's context, in its own process, receiving the tool input as JSON on stdin. Only the deny reason crosses back into the conversation, either ending the turn with a warning line or being returned to Claude as a tool error.
answers.lifecycle: Fires before every matching tool call, in every permission mode including `bypassPermissions` and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, and is unaffected by compaction because nothing about it lives in the context window. It stops only when the settings entry is removed or `disableAllHooks` is set at the same or a higher scope.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for the call it blocks, but the hook script itself can fail open: a script that is not executable, throws, or does not decompose compound commands like `cd repo && git push` lets the push through. It also only covers pushes made through Claude Code, so the real guarantee is a server-side protected-branch rule with this hook as the local backstop.
answers.version_caveat: No feature flag on PreToolUse deny. `continueOnBlock: true` (v2.1.210 or later) decides whether the deny reason ends the turn or is handed back to Claude as a tool error so it can adjust; before v2.1.210 the reason was always returned and the turn continued. In managed settings, managed hooks keep running unless `disableAllHooks` is set there too, and `allowManagedHooksOnly` blocks user and project hooks from interfering.

answers.primary: A model-invoked reference skill, for example .claude/skills/legacy-billing-context/SKILL.md with `user-invocable: false` and a description naming the real billing trigger phrases; keep SKILL.md itself a short navigation page and put the states, invariants and traps in supporting files it points at so the bulk loads only when Claude actually needs it.
answers.rejected_alternative: A .claude/rules/ entry. Rules load unconditionally at launch, or on a path match, which is exactly the always-resident cost a long explainer cannot afford, and rules have no way to be hidden from the command menu because they were never in it.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. It decides, purely from the description text, whether the conversation is about billing and the skill should load.
answers.context_boundary: Only the name and description occupy the skill listing in the main context. On invocation the rendered body enters the main conversation and persists for the session; the referenced detail files stay on disk until Claude reads them.
answers.lifecycle: Loads automatically when Claude matches the description to the current conversation, and never from the `/` menu because it is hidden there. It stops applying if `skillOverrides` sets it to `"name-only"` or `"off"`, or if the skill-listing budget truncates the description that makes it discoverable.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory and fails open, and the failure is silent: if the description misses the words people actually use, the skill never loads and Claude reasons about billing from the code alone with no signal that background context was skipped. Note that `user-invocable: false` only hides the menu entry; it does not block Skill-tool access, so use `disable-model-invocation` if the goal were the opposite.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate on `user-invocable`. The combined `description` plus `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters (tunable with `skillListingMaxDescChars`) and the whole listing shares a budget of about 1% of the model's context window (`skillListingBudgetFraction` or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET), with least-used descriptions dropped first, so the billing keywords must come first in the description.

answers.primary: A managed-policy CLAUDE.md deployed to the managed settings location (/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md on macOS, /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md on Linux and WSL, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md on Windows) via MDM, Group Policy or Ansible, or equivalently the `claudeMd` key inside managed-settings.json.
answers.rejected_alternative: Pushing a `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` to every machine with configuration management. It lands in the developer's own directory where it can be edited, excluded or deleted between config runs, so there is no non-opt-out guarantee.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split. The harness owns loading: a managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded by `claudeMdExcludes`, and the `claudeMd` key is honored only from managed and policy settings, so setting it in user or project settings does nothing. The model still owns whether the data-handling and style guidance is followed.
answers.context_boundary: Loads first in the CLAUDE.md hierarchy into the main conversation, ahead of user and project files, and also reaches every subagent that loads CLAUDE.md, which is all of them except the built-in Explore and Plan agents.
answers.lifecycle: Applies to every Claude Code session on the machine, in every repository, from the moment the policy file is distributed, and stops only when IT changes or removes it. Nothing in a session, and no individual setting, can turn it off.
answers.failure_mode: The loading half fails closed (a developer genuinely cannot opt out) while the content half stays advisory and fails open (nothing verifies compliance). Anything that must be technically enforced, such as blocking a tool, a path or a command, belongs in managed `permissions.deny`, `sandbox` settings, or a managed PreToolUse hook, not in the CLAUDE.md text.
answers.version_caveat: No version gate on managed CLAUDE.md itself, but it is honored only in the managed or policy settings scope. To close the enforcement gap and stop developers routing around it, pair it with managed-only keys such as `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `disableBypassPermissionsMode`, and `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`; on Windows, `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` is needed for WSL to read the Windows policy chain.
